subject: English
description: High-hit preposition errors and idiomatic phrasal verbs

questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is 'fond OF'. Similarly: afraid of, jealous of, aware of, capable of, proud of.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: He has been living in Delhi ____ 2010.
questions.explanation: Use 'since' with a point in time (since 2010, since Monday). Use 'for' with duration (for 15 years, for a decade). 'From' needs an end-point ('from 2010 to 2020').
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct preposition: The meeting was postponed ____ next Monday.
questions.explanation: Postpone TO a future time. ('Postpone UNTIL next Monday' is equally correct.) 'On Monday' fits 'scheduled on Monday' but not 'postponed ___ Monday'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the phrasal verb 'BEAR WITH' correctly?

options.option_text: Please bear with me while I set up the projector.
She bore with a son last year.
The bridge cannot bear with the weight.
He bore with the trophy proudly.

questions.explanation: 'Bear with (someone)' = be patient with someone. 'Bear a child' uses plain bear. 'Bear the weight' = support the weight (no 'with'). 'Bear the trophy' — the trophy is just carried; no 'with'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Identify the sentence with the correct preposition:

options.option_text: She is married with a doctor.
She is married to a doctor.
She is married by a doctor.
She is married for a doctor.

questions.explanation: 'Married TO' is the standard collocation in formal English for the spouse. 'Married with X' refers to HAVING X — 'married with two children'. 'Married BY' refers to the officiant ('married by the priest').
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: The phrasal verb 'PUT UP WITH' most nearly means:
questions.explanation: 'Put up with' = tolerate, endure reluctantly. Example: 'I can't put up with this noise any longer.' Do NOT confuse with: 'put up' = display/raise; 'put off' = postpone; 'put down' = criticise / write down.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Spot the sentence with the INCORRECT preposition:

options.option_text: He is jealous from his brother's success.
She congratulated me on my promotion.

questions.explanation: Correct: 'jealous OF his brother's success' — not 'from'. The other three are correct idiomatic collocations: accused OF, suffer FROM, congratulate (somebody) ON (something).
questions.subject: English
